question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{3}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{3},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{\sqrt{7}-\sqrt{3}} & = \\ \frac{6}{\sqrt{7}-\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{3}} & = \\ \frac{6(\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{3})}{(\sqrt{7}-\sqrt{3})(\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{3})} & = \\ \text{ }\frac{6(\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{3})}{(\sqrt{7})^{2}-(\sqrt{3})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{6(\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{3})}{7-3} & = \\ \frac{6(\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{3})}{4} & = \\ \frac{3(\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{3})}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
